{{Short description|German mathematician (1920–2016)}}
[[File:Gaschuetz.jpg|thumb|{{center|Wolfgang Gaschütz 1973}}]]
'''Wolfgang Gaschütz''' (11 June 1920 – 7 November 2016)<ref>{{cite news|url=http://lebenswege.faz.net/traueranzeige/prof-dr-dr-hc-wolfgang-gaschutz/48429881|title=''Wir trauern um Prof. Dr. Dr. hc Wolfgang Gaschütz ... Gudrun Gaschütz und Familie''|newspaper=[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]] (FAZ)|date=12 November 2016}} (obituary notice)</ref> was a German mathematician, known for his research in [[group theory]], especially the theory of [[finite group]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Laue, Hartmut|title=Wolfgang Gaschütz: Life and Work|year=2018|volume=5|pages=125–138|journal=[[Advances in Group Theory and Applications]]|url=http://www.advgrouptheory.com/journal/Volumes/5/H.%20Laue%20-%20Wolfgang%20Gaschuts%20life%20and%20work.pdf|archive-date=2020-11-24|access-date=2023-10-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124222354/http://www.advgrouptheory.com/journal/Volumes/5/H.%20Laue%20-%20Wolfgang%20Gaschuts%20life%20and%20work.pdf|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref><ref name=bio>{{MacTutor|id=Gaschutz|title=Wolfgang Gaschütz}} (article written by L. A. Shemetkov & R. Schmidt)</ref>

==Biography==
Gaschütz was born on 11 June 1920 in [[Karlshof]], [[Oderbruch]]. He moved with his family in 1931 to Berlin, where he completed his ''[[Abitur]]'' in 1938. He served as an artillery officer in WW II, which ended for him in 1945 near Kiel. There in autumn 1945 he matriculated at the [[University of Kiel]].<ref name=bio/> He was inspired by [[Andreas Speiser]]'s book ''Die Theorie der Gruppen von endlicher Ordnung''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Gaschutz_path/ |title=''My Path'' by Wolfgang Gaschütz |website=MacTutor }} (translation by Stefanie Eminger of Gaschütz's ''Mein Weg'', Proc. F. Scorina Gomel State Univ. No. 3, 2000, 7–10)</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Reviews of Andreas Speiser's books|website=MacTutor|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Speiser_Andreas_books/}}</ref> Gaschütz received his Ph.D. ([[Doctorate#Germany|''Promotion'']]) in 1949 under the supervision of [[Karl-Heinrich Weise]] with doctoral dissertation entitled  ''(Zur <math>\Phi</math>-Untergruppe endlicher Gruppen)''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=21552|name=Wolfgang Gaschütz}}</ref> In 1953 Gaschütz completed his habilitation in Kiel.<ref name=bio/> At the University of Kiel he held the junior academic appointments ''Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft'' from 1949 to 1956 and ''Diätendozent'' from 1956 to 1959. He was [[Academic ranks in Germany|''Außerplanmäßiger Professor'']] from 1959 to 1962, professor extraordinarius from 1962 to 1964, and professor ordinarius (full professor) from 1964 to 1988. He taught at Kiel until his retirement as professor emeritus in 1988.<ref name=Kiel>{{cite web|url=http://gelehrtenverzeichnis.de/person/4f068ff8-a6b5-1bb6-463f-4e37f45f872f|title=Wolfgang Gaschütz (Akademische Karriere)|website=Kieler Gelehrtenverzeichnis (Kiel Directory of Scholars)|date=11 June 1920 }}</ref> He rejected calls to Karlsruhe and Mainz. He was a visiting professor at various universities in Europe ([[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College London]] 1965 and 1970, [[University of Padua]] 1966, [[University of Florence]] 1971, [[University of Naples Federico II]] 1974, [[University of Warwick]] 1967, 1973 and 1977); in the USA ([[Michigan State University]] 1963, [[ University of Chicago]] 1968); and in Australia ([[Australian National University]] in Canberra).<ref name=Kiel/>

Gaschütz created a school of group theorists in Kiel, where there had been a gap in mathematical expertise in algebra since the death of [[Ernst Steinitz]] in 1928. Gaschütz, influenced by [[Helmut Wielandt]] in the 1950s, is best known for his research on [[Frattini subgroup]]s, on questions of complementability, on [[group cohomology]], and on the theory of finite [[solvable group]]s.<ref name=bio/> In 1959 he gave a formula for the Eulerian function<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gaschütz, W.|year=1959|title=Die Eulersche funktion endlicher auflösbarer gruppen|journal=Illinois Journal of Mathematics|volume=3|issue=4|pages=469–476|doi=10.1215/ijm/1255455454 |doi-access=free}}</ref> introduced in 1936 by [[Philip Hall]]<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1093/qmath/os-7.1.134|url=https://academic.oup.com/qjmath/article-abstract/os-7/1/134/1586928 |title=The Eulerian Functions of a Group |date=1936 |last1=Hall |first1=P. |journal=The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |pages=134–151 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and determined the number of generators of a finite solvable group in terms of structure and embedding of the chief factors of the Eulerian function.<ref name=bio/>

In 1962, Gaschütz published his theory of [[Formation (group theory)|formations]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gaschütz | first1=Wolfgang | title=Zur Theorie der endlichen auflösbaren Gruppen | mr=0179257 | year=1962 | journal=[[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] | issn=0025-5874 | volume=80 | pages=300–305 | doi=10.1007/BF01162386| s2cid=116064482 }}</ref> giving a unified theory of [[Hall subgroup]]s and [[Carter subgroup]]s. Gaschütz's theory is important for understanding finite solvable groups. He characterized solvable [[T-group (mathematics)|T-group]]s.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lqyCjUFY6WAC&pg=PA406 |page=406 |title=A Course in the Theory of Groups | isbn=9780387944616 | last1=Robinson | first1=Derek |author-link=Derek J. S. Robinson |date=1996 | publisher=Springer }}</ref> He is one of the pioneers of the theory of Fitting classes begun by [[Bernd Fischer (mathematician)|Bernd Fischer]] in 1966<ref name=bio/> and the theory of Schunk classes.<ref>{{cite book|author=Wenbin, Guo|title=The Theory of Classes of Groups|publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers|year=2000|isbn=0-7923-6268-3|chapter=Preface|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JRFmzTsjoNEC&pg=PR8|pages=viii–ix}} Updated & revised translation of the original Chinese publication, Science Press, Beijing. </ref>

Gaschütz organized the [[Mathematical Research Institute Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] conferences on group theory for many years with [[Bertram Huppert]] and [[Karl W. Gruenberg]]. In 2000 Gaschütz received an honorary doctorate from [[Francisk Skorina Gomel State University]] in [[Belarus]].<ref name=bio/> His doctoral students include Joachim Neubüser.<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Neubuser|title=Joachim Neubüser}}</ref>

Gaschütz and his wife Gudrun were married in 1943 and became the parents of a son and two daughters.<ref name=bio/>

Gaschütz died in [[Kiel]] on 7 November 2016, at the age of 96.

* ''Über die <math>\Phi</math>-Untergruppe endlicher Gruppen'', Mathematische Zeitschrift, vol. 58, 1953, pp. 160–170, [http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=GDZPPN002383535 Online] {{doi|10.1007/BF01174137}}
* {{cite journal|doi=10.1515/crll.1961.208.73 |title=A note on the modular representations of solvable groups |date=1961 |last1=Fong |first1=P. |last2=Gaschütz |first2=W. |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |volume=208 |pages=73–78 |s2cid=118368313 }}
* ''Praefrattinigruppen'', Archiv der Mathematik, vol. 13, 1962, pp. 418–426. {{doi|10.1007/BF01650090}}
* ''Zur Theorie der endlichen auflösbaren Gruppen'', Mathematische Zeitschrift, vol. 80, 1963, pp. 300–305, [http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=GDZPPN002392380 Online]
* {{cite journal|doi=10.1515/crll.1970.245.172 |title=On presentations of finite p-groups |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |date=1970 |volume=245 |pages=172–176 |s2cid=117732425 }}
* {{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01110166 |title=Sylowisatoren |date=1971 |last1=Gaschütz |first1=Wolfgang |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |volume=122 |issue=4 |pages=319–320 }}
* {{cite journal|doi=10.1515/crll.1977.295.214 |title=Subgroup criteria for an abelian group |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |date=1977 |volume=295 |pages=214–220 |s2cid=120015921 }}
* [https://books.google.com/books/about/Lectures_on_Subgroups_of_Sylow_Type_in_F.html?id=fOzuAAAAMAAJ ''Lectures on subgroups of Sylow type in finite soluble groups''], Canberra, Australian National University 1979 {{LCCN|80509698}} {{isbn|0908160224}} (pbk.)
